passages.P2: # Joe Biden family death: verified facts and context
passages.P8: Public reports have referenced deaths in former President Joe Biden’s family, including the passing of a daughter as a child, the death of his first wife and a child in a car accident in 1972, and the death of his son Beau Biden in 2015. This status clarifier summarizes confirmed details and provides context for each reported family death linked to Joe Biden, emphasizing dates, relationships, and verifiable information available from authoritative sources.
passages.P9: ## Key family death events tied to Joe Biden
passages.P10: ### 1972 car accident: Neilia Biden and Naomi Biden
passages.P11: In December 1972, then-Senator Joe Biden’s first wife, Neilia Biden, and their youngest daughter, Naomi Biden, were killed in a head-on car collision in Delaware. Their sons, Beau and Hunter, were also in the vehicle and were injured. This event is a defining biographical detail of Joe Biden’s early public life and is widely documented in news archives and official remembrances.
passages.P13: Joseph R. Biden III, commonly known as Beau Biden, died in May 2015 after a battle with brain cancer. Beau served as Attorney General of Delaware and was widely noted for his public service and resilience during his illness. His death was publicly acknowledged by Joe Biden and covered extensively in reliable media.

passages.P1: # Hunter Biden now living abroad as legal troubles mount, court filing reveals
passages.P2:
By Latest & Breaking News on Fox News
Apr 15, 2026 | 4:18 PM
passages.P3: Embattled former first son Hunter Biden has reportedly moved out of the United States amid mounting legal issues, just a year after his father left the presidential office in 2025.
passages.P4: His attorney, Barry Coburn, disclosed Biden’s current living situation in an April 6 court filing tied to a civil lawsuit over unpaid legal fees.
passages.P5: “Mr. Biden lives abroad,” the document stated. “He cannot pay his current lawyers.”
passages.P6: It remains unclear where the first son of former President Joe Biden has relocated. However, the 56-year-old previously indicated late last year that he had been visiting Cape Town in South Africa, where his wife, Melissa Cohen Biden, is originally from.
passages.P7: “When all of the political and personal stuff came to an end in the last six months, I had always promised that we would spend some time over here,” Biden said during a November appearance on The Wide Awake Podcast, based in South Africa. “We’re trying to be between Cape Town and the States, go back and forth.”
passages.P8: “I’ve fallen madly in love with Cape Town,” he added. “You guys do not know how good you have it here. It’s the most beautiful city in the world.”
passages.P9: Most recently, Biden was photographed with his family — alongside his parents, Joe Biden and Jill Biden — in Santa Ynez, California, over Easter weekend, according to photos shared on Instagram last week by his sister, Ashley Biden.
passages.P10: The court document disclosing Biden’s current living situation was submitted in a Washington, D.C., civil court by Winston & Strawn LLP, which previously represented him in a series of criminal cases that drew intense national scrutiny over the years, including a felony gun trial in Delaware and a tax crimes prosecution in California.
passages.P11: According to the filings, the former first son has not paid a “substantial portion” of the fees owed to his legal team. He reportedly has limited financial resources and also cannot afford to hire specialized professionals to assist with the lawsuit, citing instances that Biden manually “hand-searched” his own emails to locate relevant documents rather than relying on outside resources.
passages.P12: Biden also noted during his podcast appearance that he is facing “$17 million in debt … as it relates to my legal fees.”
passages.P13: In summer 2024, Biden was found guilty of multiple criminal offenses, including the illegal purchase of a firearm in 2018. Prosecutors proved he lied on a federal form by stating he was not using illegal drugs at a time when he was struggling with a crack cocaine addiction.
passages.P14: He also pleaded guilty to nine federal tax charges, including three felonies, in connection with a scheme to evade $1.4 million in taxes between 2016 and 2019.
passages.P15: He was ultimately pardoned by his father on all federal charges in December 2024.

passages.P1: # Hunter Biden Left the United States After Father's Term as President, Lawyer Reveals
passages.P2: A recent court filing stated that the former first son now "lives abroad," just a year after President Joe Biden left the White House
passages.P6: Joseph Konig is Writer-Reporter on the Current Events team at PEOPLE. He first joined the brand in 2026.
passages.P11:
Hunter Biden and his wife Melissa Cohen Biden on Jan. 17, 2025.
Credit :
passages.P14:
* Hunter Biden is living outside the United States just over a year after his father left the White House, his lawyer revealed in a court filing last week
* It’s not clear where Biden, 56, has relocated, but in a November 2025 podcast interview, he said he was splitting time between the U.S. and Cape Town, South Africa
* His wife, Melissa Cohen Biden, originally hails from South Africa
passages.P15: Hunter Biden is living outside the United States just over a year after his father left the White House, his lawyer revealed in a court filing last week.
passages.P16: His attorney, Barry Coburn, filed a 14-page document on April 6 in a civil lawsuit over unpaid legal fees that mentions, “Mr. Biden lives abroad.” Coburn declined to offer more detail when reached by PEOPLE.
passages.P17: It’s not clear where in the world Hunter, 56, has relocated to, but in a November 2025 podcast interview, he said he was splitting time between the U.S. and Cape Town, South Africa.
passages.P18: His wife, Melissa Cohen Biden, originally hails from South Africa. They had been living in California since they got married in 2019, Biden said.
passages.P19: “When all the all of the political and personal stuff came to an end in the last six months, I had always promised that we would spend some time over here,” Hunter said on the South Africa-based *Wide Awake Podcast*. “I've fallen madly in love with Cape Town. You guys do not know how good you have it here. It’s the most beautiful city in the world.”
passages.P20: Hunter also noted in that interview that most of the houses around the home he rented in Malibu, Calif., were burned down in the 2024 Palisades fire, “so we can’t go back anyway.”
passages.P21: President Donald Trump revoked Secret Service protection early for Hunter and his sister Ashley Biden in March 2025 because of photos taken of Hunter in South Africa, whose government Trump has falsely accused of enabling a genocide of white farmers.
passages.P22: “Hunter Biden has had Secret Service protection for an extended period of time, all paid for by the United States Taxpayer. There are as many as 18 people on this Detail, which is ridiculous!” Trump wrote on March 17, 2025, on his Truth Social platform. “He is currently vacationing in, of all places, South Africa, where the Human Rights of people has been strenuously questioned.”
passages.P23: Marking the conclusion of his first year back in office on Jan. 20, Trump's White House provided reporters with a packet of “365 wins” in the first 365 days, including #243: “stripped notorious crackhead and grifter Hunter Biden of his taxpayer-funded Secret Service detail.”
passages.P24: Hunter was with his family, including former President Joe Biden and former first lady Jill Biden, in Santa Ynez, Calif., earlier this month celebrating Easter, photos shared by Ashley on Instagram showed.

records.title: A court filing submitted on April 6, 2026, by Hunter Biden's ...
records.retrieval_query: Search for a primary court filing or docket entry (e.g., the April 6 filing by Barry Coburn) that independently documents Hunter Biden's living status, rather than news retellings of it.

passages.P1: A court filing submitted on April 6, 2026, by Hunter Biden’s attorney Barry Coburn in a Washington, D.C. lawsuit from his former law firm Winston & Strawn states that Hunter Biden now “lives abroad” and “cannot afford” to pay his outstanding legal bills.
passages.P2: The firm claims he owes fees “substantially in excess of $50,000” related to his prior tax and gun cases. The filing describes him as “impecunious” (penniless) and notes that neither he nor his current lawyers can cover discovery costs such as billing consultants or e-discovery vendors.
passages.P3: This aligns with Hunter Biden’s own earlier statements claiming roughly $17 million (about ₹158 crore) in debt, mostly from legal expenses tied to his federal cases. Some media reports describe him as having “quietly bolted” from the U.S., though the filing itself simply states he lives abroad without specifying the location or suggesting he is evading authorities.
